no-var  This is a `var` declaration, which is function-scoped and hoisted rather than block-scoped. nexus/consistency-no-for-in  Iterate an object with `for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(object))`, or `Object.keys(object)` when only the key matters, rather than `for...in`. `for...in` walks the prototype chain, so it needs a guard to be correct, and a guard is a line someone forgets; it also hands back every key as a bare `string`, which is why these loops grow `key as keyof typeof object` casts to read the value. `Object.entries` returns own keys only, with the value already in hand, so there is nothing to guard and nothing to cast, and every loop over an object has one shape.

no-var  This is a `var` declaration, which is function-scoped and hoisted rather than block-scoped. The binding exists from the top of the enclosing function, so it is readable above the line that declares it and it leaks out of the block it looks like it belongs to: a `var` inside an `if` is still in scope after the `if` ends. A `var` in a loop is one binding shared by every iteration, which is why a closure created in the loop sees the final value rather than its own. Use `let`, or `const` when nothing reassigns it.
